correctness.rationale: In the stationary environment the elapsed current plateau length L is Exp(ν), independent of its mark λ and the path prior to that plateau. If T is a particle's last-reset age, write u=E[T|path], v=E[T²|path]/2. Let b=e^(−λL), a=(1−b)/λ, g=∫₀ᴸ t e^(−λt)dt. Integrating the conditional survival gives u=a+b u_old and v=g+Lb u_old+b v_old; the independent earlier environment has the same backward law. Renewal finiteness holds even at unbounded or very small rates: the unit-age survival time kernel weighted by the refresh rate has mass νA<1, which remains <1 after a sufficiently small exponential tilt, yielding finite age moments. Averaging the first recursion, its square, and the second gives E u=A/S, E u²=2C/(SR), E v=A₂/S² (in particular E[a²]=2C and E[ab]=νC). Conditional independence makes the square-product moment (2D)² E u², whereas the one-particle fourth moment is 24D² E v by the Gaussian fourth moment. Hence the stated quotient and zero positional covariance by sign symmetry. The squared covariance is (2D)² Var(u), strictly positive when varying a nondegenerate current mark on a positive-length plateau and zero for a point mass. Conditional Jensen gives 3E[X₁²X₂²]≤E[X₁⁴], with strict correlation bound <1/3 after subtracting the positive squared mean. For −1<α<1, λ=νt gives A₂∼cν^(α−1)K and C∼cν^(α−1)J using integrable scaled kernels; the tail away from zero is O(1). νA,νB→0 and A²/A₂→0 by the three bounds O(ν^α), O(log(1/ν)), O(1) on A according to the sign of α. Splitting J's kernel as ∫₁/₂¹ da/(t+a)² gives J/K=∫₁/₂¹ a^(α−1)da, including log 2 at α=0. This decreases from 1 to 1/2 across the open interval, so the limit is in (1/6,1/3). The E₁ example follows by shifting the exponential-rate integrals, partial fractions for C and integration by parts for A₂. An independent rational plateau-recursion computation on a three-state law reproduced the moments and ρ≈0.0753581604463, 0.0552138058996, 0.0115187376429 at ν=1/19,4/5,9.
residual_risks: The rational check is discrete and cannot establish the density asymptotic; the scaled integral proof covers the latter. Neither result asserts convergence of the full joint position law, nor a finite-moment ν=0 law. The density limit is not claimed at α=±1.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Arbitrary waiting-time laws do not broaden a shared clock into two independent ones. The one-body refresh solution checks marginal ingredients but does not compute the joint expectation of two conditional age means. The primary search yielded no decisive additional theorem, not evidence that none exists.

evidence: Either separately timed reset kills the product, giving mixed loss 2λ instead of λ under simultaneous resetting. The resulting mixed integral E[(λ+ν)^−1(2λ+ν)^−1] and its comparison with the marginal fourth moment yield distinct scaled kernels.
A stationary one-body law, even exactly known, is compatible with different joint reset clocks and cannot fix this mixed-moment calculation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Generic conditioning establishes the covariance mechanism and the one-body law overlaps marginal calculations. An additional joint calculation and an asymptotic normalization by two diverging moments are needed for the stated universal law.

evidence: Boyer–Majumdar §II uses the same type of Pearson observable; §III gives simultaneous memory resets.
Resultary 78bed4679cd8 is an individual-reset pair correlation in a shared diffusivity environment, not a shared hazard.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Conditioning on the rate trajectory here yields two independent reset ages and the covariance of their conditional means. A simultaneous protocol yields one shared random age or shared reset-to-past event, and shared diffusivity instead correlates integrated variance. Those are not mathematical equivalents.

originality.rationale: Credit the Poisson-redraw environment and its one-particle law to Arutkin–Reuveni and the conditional-independence mechanism to prior methods. The distinct supported claim is the exact stationary squared-displacement correlation for separate conditional clocks and its explicit slow-refresh family over all specified near-zero density exponents. The strongest checked model and observable matches do not determine that pair result.
residual_risks: An unindexed or more general two-body Markov-modulated Cox calculation could overlap the stationary moment identity. The broad web lookup was nondecisive. This is a best-of-knowledge comparison, not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: Separately timed resets do not eliminate environmental correlations. The exact joint observable separates a zero signed covariance from strict fourth-order dependence and distinguishes shared hazards from shared events. Its slow-refresh ratio sorts an entire continuum of low-rate laws despite divergent fourth moments, independently of the rest of the rate distribution. This gives an interpretable benchmark not obtained by just substituting an exponential density into a one-particle formula.
residual_risks: Value claimed only for the stationary Poisson-redraw model and the specified moment ratio, not broad universality for arbitrary correlated environments.
